Training Progression Duration (T) differentiates between regimens, suggesting that extended preparation periods yield superior physiological adaptations. These operators form a dualistic structure: one rooted in static physical traits and another in dynamic developmental timelines. Failure modes include insufficient chest girth leading to respiratory compromise, poor body composition causing inefficiency, and abbreviated training periods resulting in subpar conditioning. Each primitive operates within a defined regime—C > 36, W/H optimal, T > 20 weeks—and their intersection defines elite rowing readiness.
